items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Panama Francis did some of the sides, and Mosey Alexander did the other side... And Milt Hinton, Panama Francis on drums... We went down to Uruguay to play for the festival down there

ctx.x: So Panama Francis was in that and this boy, Pretty Eddie, the drummer, he was Panama's understudy there. We did -- then we did another show with Dennis O'Keefe called 'Never Sleep Over a Pretzel Factory' right after that, then Max the Mirror or Max Cavulli had a place out in Brooklyn, and we used to play -- called Max the Mirror -- we used to play out there.

And then there was another job, Snaghead's Inn, and we -- I did some records with Dick Vance and Benny Morton on my own, you know, with the -- and then there was a play -- I was with a guy yesterday called Awfully Nice that I conducted. We went up to New Haven and up to Philly. It didn't go very far.

items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: I open at Michael's Pub on August 28th with Eddie Woodie Barefield.

ctx.x: Panama is finishing an engagement down here, and he's returning to New York to open at Michael's Pub. When are you going to Michael's Pub, Panama?
I open at Michael's Pub on August 28th with Eddie Woodie Barefield.

With Eddie Woodie Barefield, huh? Great. Well, man, I tell you -- it was a joy seeing your lovely place, and to see how great success has been for you down here all through this music business. Considering the troubles and what the music business is like, this is really a joy to see.
